note: مدد centrally means help/aid/assistance. Relief and reinforcement can occur contextually, but 'supply' is not an appropriate standalone core gloss.
بے is primarily a productive privative prefix meaning without-/un-/-less; the letter-name homograph is a noun. Adjective POS is misleading.
proposed_english: without-; un-; -less; non-; name of the letter ب (context-dependent)

note: دوسرے is the masculine plural/oblique form of دوسرا meaning second or other. 'Closed-class' hides its adjectival/determiner role.
proposed_english: second; other (masculine plural/oblique form of دوسرا)

note: پیش functions adverbially/noun-like in expressions meaning before/in front/forward and can mean presented/offered; it is also the Urdu name of the damma vowel mark. Adjective/noun alone is incomplete.
proposed_english: before; in front; forward; presented/offered; pesh/damma vowel mark

note: مختلف centrally means different/various. The current gloss omits 'different' and leads with less useful 'other/opposed'.
ہمارے is a possessive determiner/pronoun form meaning our/ours, masculine plural or oblique. 'Closed-class' is too vague.
پانی centrally means water. Sweat/tears can be described with پانی in compounds or figurative uses, while 'alcohol' is not a safe core learner gloss.
proposed_english: water; liquid/moisture; tears or sweat (in compounds/context-dependent)

note: دوران means duration/course/period and is widely used in کے دوران 'during'. 'Content word' is not a grammatical POS.
proposed_english: duration; course; period; during (in کے دوران)

note: بڑی should give a direct learner meaning instead of only saying it is the feminine of بڑا.
proposed_english: big; large; elder/older; great (feminine form of بڑا, context-dependent)

note: مجھے should directly tell a learner 'me/to me' rather than only describe it as the dative/accusative of میں.
ایسے means such/like this/in this way and functions as a demonstrative/adjectival or adverbial form. 'Closed-class' is too vague.
proposed_english: such; like this/that; in this way

note: موجود centrally means present/existing/available. 'Ready, willing' is not a normal standalone modern learner meaning and should not be taught as core.
کھیل should lead with game/sport/play/fun. 'Scheme, plan' is peripheral/idiomatic and risks confusing a beginner.
proposed_english: game; sport; play; fun; easy matter/task (idiomatic, context-dependent)

note: بلکہ is a conjunction/discourse connector meaning rather/but rather/in fact/moreover, not merely an adverb.
proposed_english: rather; but rather; in fact; moreover

note: نظر means sight/view/look/gaze and can mean opinion/attention/supervision in constructions. 'Eye' alone is more properly آنکھ and should not lead the learner entry.
proposed_english: sight; view; look; gaze; opinion; attention/supervision (context-dependent)

note: جہاں is the relative/interrogative adverb 'where/wherever'. 'Beloved' is spurious dictionary noise (likely contamination from جان or a name) and noun POS is misleading here.
میرے is the masculine plural/oblique possessive form of میرا and functions as possessive determiner/pronoun. 'Closed-class' is too vague.
مگر is a conjunction meaning but/however/except or unless in some constructions. Noun POS is unexplained dictionary noise for this learner entry.
پاس means near/nearby/by and is central in کے پاس to express possession ('with/have'). The current one-word gloss is too narrow.
proposed_english: near; nearby; by; with/in someone's possession (in کے پاس)
